clue.text: A lot of straddling by sporty types here?

definitions.text: A lot of straddling by sporty types here?

blocks.clueFragment: A lot of straddling by sporty types here?
blocks.note: surface reading: a racy hint at some athletic bedroom romping
setter's reading: skiers sit astride a T-bar or button tow as it drags them up the slope, and many of them do so at once

explanation.surface: A nudge-nudge suggestion that athletic people get up to a great deal of straddling somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye's Cyclops loves a smutty surface; the innocent reading is a mountain tow that winter-sports fans ride with legs either side of a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow on the slopes carries winter-sports enthusiasts uphill, many of them perched astride a bar.

clue.text: Screw Nick!

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for having sex with someone
second meaning: to steal, British slang for pinching something

explanation.walkthrough: The capital N makes Nick look like a man's name being propositioned; it is the British slang verb for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is British slang both for having sex with someone and for stealing goods, just as screw and nick are.

clue.text: Nigel at last has merit? Get wise!

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before it, nothing else

blocks.note: the final letter of the name
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A sarcastic jibe asking whether Nigel finally deserves praise, and telling him to smarten up.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wise to something is to come to know it, which is what acquiring knowledge or being taught amounts to.

clue.text: Bustle fitted to Kitty the nit-picker

blocks.note: bustle and fuss both mean busy, agitated activity
a kitty is a shared pool of money, a pot

explanation.surface: Someone attaching a dress bustle to a person or cat called Kitty, who is a pedant.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty reads as a name or a cat; it is the pool of money in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who frets over tiny details and finds fault with trivial things is a classic petty worrier.

clue.text: Sophisticated, switching front to back with an erection? Bit of a malfunction!

indicators.note: the opening letter is lifted off and moved to the tail of the word

blocks.note: chic means stylish and sophisticated
an erection is something standing up

explanation.surface: A smooth seducer whose arousal goes embarrassingly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is a minor hitch or temporary setback, a small glitch in proceedings.

clue.text: Would you believe it? Wavering Ukip, power lost, say nothing

indicators.note: power is the physics symbol P, and lost means that letter goes
something wavering is unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: the party name with its power symbol removed
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An exasperated aside about Ukip wobbling, losing its strength and saying nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ukip was the UK Independence Party, Nigel Farage's anti-EU party.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief or exasperation, used when something seems scarcely credible.

clue.text: Cold CIA prick almost involved with Zero caper

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
the word without its last letter
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A frosty CIA agent caught up in some nothing escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a lively, whimsical piece or a frolic, so it can mean a prank or playful escapade.

clue.text: Abrasive stuff stuffed up timid sorts

indicators.note: stuffed in the sense of ruined or messed about, so the little word gets jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
timid people are often called mice

explanation.surface: Something rough being crammed into shy, retiring people.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffed up looks like a phrase; stuffed is the signal and up is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is light volcanic rock used for scrubbing and polishing, a scouring material.

clue.text: Which reveals the goings-on of royals having romance with flier

definitions.text: Which reveals the goings-on of royals

blocks.note: to romance someone is to court them
a flier is a leaflet handed out, a circular

explanation.surface: Royal scandal: someone in the family is having an affair with a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier reads as an aviator; it is a printed leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the daily record printed in British newspapers listing the official engagements of members of the royal family.

clue.text: Brenda for one, wanting sex, beds a whole regiment

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, an example of a royal
S stands for sex, as in the age/sex/location shorthand on forms and chat
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: The Queen, feeling frisky, takes an entire regiment to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Scots was the oldest infantry regiment of the British Army, so the name denotes a complete military unit.

clue.text: see 24ac.
see 23ac.
Labour scrap provides a bit of impromptu entertainment?

blocks.note: Labour is a political party
a scrap is a piece of something

explanation.surface: A Labour Party squabble turns into accidental comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap reads as a fight; it is a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a turn someone performs to entertain guests when called on, such as a song or trick.

clue.text: Make up for Dicky getting fix

blocks.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, off
to fix something in place is to set it

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky gets a fix and must make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; in British slang a dicky heart or tummy is one that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance or compensate for it.

clue.text: Sting with annoying twit's brain

blocks.note: to sting is to smart with pain
arse is British slang for an irritating fool

explanation.surface: The singer Sting paired with the brains of some irritating idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting is the rock singer in the surface. Brain is meant sarcastically, as when someone is called a brainbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all who shows off their cleverness is mockingly called a brain or a clever clogs.

clue.text: Conservative to stand for election – origins of Cameron's historic crisis

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so only the opening letters of the following words count

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
to stand for office is to run
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Tory standing for office amid the start of David Cameron's historic crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A crunch is a critical moment or decisive point, as in a credit crunch or crunch time.

clue.text: Gives the willies less shaking when slapper recruited

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things about, so the letters are rearranged
recruited means taken in, so one piece is enlisted inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
slapper and tart are both British slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A smutty line about genitals shaking less once a loose woman joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: Willies is British slang for penises, but to give someone the willies is to make them nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the willies is to frighten or alarm them, which is what a sudden shock does.

clue.text: Interfere with broadcast by jerk, which has tacky content

blocks.note: to jam a signal is to block a transmission
a jar is a jolt or jerk

explanation.surface: Some idiot disrupting a TV transmission, whose output is tacky.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacky reads as tasteless TV; it means sticky, as preserves are.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass pot holding preserves contains something sticky, so its contents are literally tacky.

clue.text: Convenience Party (English) for the average male

blocks.note: a convenience is a toilet, a john in slang
a do is a party
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A political party described as handy for the ordinary Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: A public convenience is a British euphemism for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is the placeholder for an anonymous or typical man, used for an unidentified person.

clue.text: Farage's end? Not quite – throw out the lump!

indicators.note: not quite the end means the letter just before the last one
out in the sense of disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fifth letter of the six-letter name, one short of the end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheer that Nigel Farage is nearly finished: chuck out the oaf!
explanation.walkthrough: Lump reads as an insult for a clumsy man; it is a swelling. Nigel Farage was the leader of Ukip.
explanation.definitionFit: A growth is a tumour or swelling on the body, a lump.

clue.text: Bats weigh (including energy) unknown amount – bloody hell!

indicators.note: including means taking something inside
bats as in batty or crazy, so the letters go haywire

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy
z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone weighing bats and getting a mystery figure swears in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats looks like the flying animals being weighed; it is the adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or astonishment, one mild and American, one a British oath.

clue.text: Is being impudent the makings of an arse?

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, giving lip or back-chat to someone
second meaning: the two buttocks that make up a backside

explanation.walkthrough: The question pretends that cheekiness makes you a fool; arse is the literal bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for talking back insolently and a plural noun for the buttocks.

clue.text: Old moral campaigner wants space for grand residence

blocks.note: Mary of that surname, written as one word, campaigned against sex and swearing on British television

explanation.surface: A late morals crusader needing room to move into a mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Whitehouse spelt her surname as one word; put a space in it and it becomes two words for a famous residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The official home of the US President in Washington is the most famous grand dwelling of its name.

clue.text: (&12ac.) Banker is loaded – much in evidence at a Miley performance

definitions.text: much in evidence at a Miley performance

indicators.note: loaded means drunk, and a drunk staggers about out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich banker at a raunchy Miley Cyrus concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaded looks like rich, fitting a banker; it means drunk. Miley Cyrus was notorious for near-naked performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Miley Cyrus's stage shows were famous for skimpy costumes, so exposed flesh is prominent there.

clue.text: Erection balls-up

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a stiff penis
second meaning: a silly blunder

explanation.walkthrough: Balls-up is British slang for a mess or blunder, though here it sits suggestively next to Erection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is American slang for a stiff member and also an old term for a howler or embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Which helps publican piss on untrendy shoe

blocks.note: piss is slang for weak beer
a pump is a plain canvas or slip-on shoe, hardly fashionable

explanation.surface: A crude image of someone urinating on a dowdy shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle on a bar that draws ale up from the cellar is how a publican serves customers.

clue.text: It marks the demise of Ken L. – the lad's done for

indicators.note: done for means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An obituary for some Ken L., announcing that the poor lad is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd initial in Ken L. is there to supply a letter, not to name anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolling bell rung for a death signals a passing, and figuratively anything that heralds an end.

clue.text: Crappy week had by Speaker, outwardly – "Stick it!"

indicators.note: something crappy is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
outwardly means only the outside letters are kept
had by means held by, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker, after a dreadful week, tells critics where to put it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skewer something is to pierce it with a pointed rod, literally to run a spike through it.

clue.text: East European web domain 'free' art is of the nature of Russian-style absolute rule

definitions.text: of the nature of Russian-style absolute rule

indicators.note: free means loose and unconstrained, so the letters are released into a new order

blocks.note: cz is the internet domain of the Czech Republic
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Czech website offering free art, described as autocratic.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsars ruled imperial Russia as autocrats, so the adjective describes that kind of despotic government.
